Field.name: InputFile
Field.usage: Montaged image input file to be blended
Field.manpage: Montaged image input file to be blended. All non-option arguments will also be taken as input files.

Field.name: DistortionField
Field.usage: Image distortion field file to use for undistorting images
Field.manpage: Image distortion field file to use for undistorting images. The undistortion is applied when computing edge functions.

Field.name: ImagesAreBinned
Field.usage: The current binning of the images
Field.manpage: The current binning of the images, so that the image distortion field can be applied correctly. This entry is required when doing image distortion corrections unless Blendmont can determine the binning unambiguously from the image size.

Field.name: VerySloppyMontage
Field.usage: Do correlations with parameters for finding very big displacements
Field.manpage: Do correlations with parameters for finding very big displacements. This option should generally be used for montages taken with stage movement, unless stage movements are relatively precise (e.g., at very low magnification or with a very good stage). The default is to have just the \fB-sloppy\fR option to Blendmont(1).

Field.name: RobustFitCriterion
Field.usage: Criterion for ignoring aberrant edge shifts when finding piece shifts
Field.manpage: When solving for the piece shifts from the displacements between pieces, Blendmont(1) can give less weight to, or completely ignore, displacements that appear to be outliers. This option activates this robust fitting and specifies the criterion for determining an outlier. A value of 1 will generally find nearly all outliers but may downweight some edge displacements inappropriately and give a poor blend across those edges. Higher values, up to about 1.5, will avoid the latter problem but will tend not to catch actual outliers. This option is ideal for getting a higher quality blend quickly for a low-magnification map where grid bars ruin some of the displacements. For data to be analyzed, it is preferable to fix the bad displacements or mark edges to be excluded in Midas(1). Robust fitting is available only with more than 10 pieces.

Field.name: CPUMachineList
Field.usage: Machines to use for parallel processing, or number of local cores
Field.manpage: List of machines to use for parallel processing, or simply a number of cores to use on the local machine. The entry is passed directly to Processchunks(1). Machines with multiple processors can be entered as many times as the number of processors that you want to use, or a machine name can be entered with a ":" and the number of processors to use. For example, "tubule:4,eclipse:6" would use 4 processors on tubule and 6 on eclipse.

Field.name: RemoteDirectory
Field.usage: Path to current directory on remote machines
Field.manpage: Path on remote machines to the current directory, the one where this program is being run. This would be determined by ssh'ing to the machine, cd'ing to this directory, and running pwd.

Field.name: ParallelBlend
Field.usage: Use parallel blending of individual files; assume given # of processors
Field.manpage: This option causes the program to run Blendmont(1) in parallel for each individual input file. Splitblend(1) is called with the given number as the expected number of processors. If \fB-cpus\fR is not entered, Processchunks(1) is run with the same number of processors; however, if \fB-cpus\fR is entered, it will be sent to Processchunks(1) and that determines how many processors are actually used. It is best to make the number of processors be consistent between the two entries.

Field.name: ResumeProcessing
Field.usage: Resume processing uncompleted files instead of redoing all
Field.manpage: Resume processing uncompleted files instead of redoing all files. This option cannot be used with parallel blending of individual files.

Field.name: FixEdgesInMidas
Field.usage: Open Midas for fixing alignments in overlap zones, then reblend
Field.manpage: Open Midas(1) for fixing alignments in overlap zones. This option can be used only after an initial run has created the command files. Midas will first be opened for each input file in turn, then all files will be reblended using the existing edge displacements but recomputing edge functions.

Field.name: CheckFile
Field.usage: File to check for quit and finish signals
Field.manpage: File to check for quit and finish signals. The default is "justblend.cmds" in the directory where this program is run. This file should not have the same name as the file used to control Processchunks(1) when it runs jobs, which is "processchunks-jb.cmds", also in the current directory. If a Q is placed in this file, it will terminate any running jobs and stop all processing. If an F is placed in the file, the program will stop after finishing the current file. A P can be used instead of F except when blending individual files in parallel.

autodoc.Field:
change FN Name of file with entries for changing Blendmont parameters
'Name of file with entries for changing Blendmont parameters. Each entry <has the form "option>value", where "option" can be any Blendmont option that does not conflict with the ones managed by this program. There can be spaces in the value. The full name of the option should be used in case the option is included in the stock command file.'

one CHM One entry for changing a Blendmont parameter
'One entry for changing a Blendmont parameter, in the format <"option">value". When entering options at the command line, the whole entry must be quoted if the value contains spaces. Entries with this option are processed after a file entered with \fB-change\fR, and later entries override earlier ones. For example,</"option> <"-one BinByFactor">2" will produce output binned by 2.'</"-one BinByFactor>
